clue.text: Trendy doctor brought to ruin

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a standard abbreviation for an army doctor
to dish someone's hopes is to wreck or ruin them

explanation.surface: A fashionable physician ends up financially ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Modish means in the current fashion, a close synonym of trendy.

clue.text: Powered, it's moored at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused or all over the place, so the preceding letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A boat tied up at its mooring turns out to have an engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges ITSMOORED, the letters of 'it's moored', ignoring the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle or boat fitted with an engine is motorised, that is, powered rather than rowed or sailed.

clue.text: Give forth notes on organ

parts.note: D and E are two notes of the musical scale
the liver is a bodily organ

explanation.surface: An organist produces notes from the instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' looks musical but is the body part. In a down clue 'on' places the notes on top of the organ.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver a speech or verdict is to utter it, to give it forth.

clue.text: Schoolboy made progress at this, according to Jaques

definitions.text: Schoolboy made progress at this, according to Jaques

parts.words: Schoolboy made progress at this, according to Jaques
parts.note: in Shakespeare's As You Like It, Jaques's 'seven ages' speech has the whining schoolboy creeping like a snail unwillingly to school, so the clue asks for the slow speed he moved at

explanation.walkthrough: Jaques is the melancholy lord in As You Like It whose 'All the world's a stage' speech describes the schoolboy 'creeping like snail unwillingly to school'.
explanation.definitionFit: A very slow rate of progress is proverbially compared to how fast a snail crawls.

clue.text: Do we turn switch to produce current? Yes

indicators.note: to switch things is to change them round, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone at an electrical switch asks whether flicking it will make the power flow, and is assured it will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch' and 'current' pretend to be electrical. 'switch' rearranges DOWETURN, the letters of 'Do we turn'; 'Yes' simply answers the question in the surface and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertow is a strong current beneath the surface of the sea, pulling away from the shore.

clue.text: Managed turnover to contain run in debt contracting

indicators.note: the reversed word holds the following letter within it
turning a word over in a down clue flips it end to end, so the synonym for managed is read backwards

parts.note: ran a business means managed it
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
someone owing money is in debt

explanation.surface: A business whose turnover once ran into debt is now shrinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like business revenue, the misdirection; it reverses the word for managed, making NAR, and 'to contain' then puts R inside, giving NARR.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrowing describes something getting smaller or tighter, a synonym of contracting.

clue.text: Cycles found in outer Asia

indicators.note: the answer is located within the letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: Patterns of history repeat themselves in remote parts of Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Eras are long periods of time, and history is often seen as a series of such cycles or ages.

clue.text: Less stout served from pub in the middle of Herts

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held and as printed: 'Less stout served from pub in the middle of Herts'. INN (pub) fits inside TH...ER, but 'Herts' supplies HERTS, not THER, and no indicator rearranges it, so the wordplay cannot honestly build the answer.
annotationWithheld.clue: Less stout served from pub in the middle of Herts

clue.text: Snatch a break, so to speak

indicators.note: this phrase signals that the word for a break is said out loud and heard as another spelling

parts.note: a rest is a break from work

explanation.surface: A busy worker grabs a few moments off.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrest is to seize or pull something away forcibly, to snatch it.

clue.text: Hurry to hide

definitions.meaning: to ... along is to run fast, to hurry

explanation.surface: Someone rushes off to go into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' reads as a verb but is the noun, an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelting means rushing at speed, and a pelt is the fur-covered skin of an animal.

clue.text: Students get state backing in commitment to field work

indicators.note: the students and the reversed state are placed inside the word for commitment

parts.note: a tie is a binding obligation or commitment
L is a learner, and two of them make students

indicators.note: going backwards, so the state's abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: Students win government support for their commitment to agricultural labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like financial support but turns the state round, making AG; 'in' then places LLAG inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is the ploughing and cultivating of land, the work done in a field.

clue.text: Recognize old' coin is English

parts.note: the real was an old silver coin of Spain and its colonies
taken as written

explanation.surface: A collector identifies an antique coin as English.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray mark after 'old' is a printing speck; the clue reads 'old coin'.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to become aware of it or understand it, to recognise it.

clue.text: Story about Continental victory an eye-opener

indicators.note: around, so the story's letters go about the victory's

parts.note: a relation is an account or narrative, a story
VE, Victory in Europe, marks the Allied win on the Continent in 1945

explanation.surface: A tale of a European triumph turns out to be surprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but means the word for story surrounds VE.
explanation.definitionFit: A revelation is a surprising disclosure, something that opens one's eyes.

clue.text: The speed of a flier

definitions.meaning: a unit of speed at sea or in the air, one nautical mile per hour
a wading bird, a sandpiper, so a creature that flies

explanation.surface: Someone asks how fast an aircraft goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' suggests a plane or pilot, but here it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships and aircraft measure velocity in nautical miles per hour, and the same word names a shore bird.

clue.text: No movement for a couple of holy men unwell

parts.note: ST is a saint, so two of them are ST and ST
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: Two monks fall sick and can no longer move.
explanation.walkthrough: The couple is written out with the joining word: ST AND ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A standstill is a halt where nothing moves at all.

clue.text: There's little weight in moral consideration

definitions.meaning: an old apothecaries' unit of weight, twenty grains
a qualm of conscience that holds one back

explanation.surface: A philosopher remarks that ethics carries little weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's' and 'in' only link the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a tiny apothecaries' measure and a pang of conscience about right and wrong.

clue.text: River crustacean to the French is abhorrent

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England
a crab is a crustacean
le is the French for the

explanation.surface: A diner finds a river crab with a French name disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Execrable means dreadful, deserving to be cursed, close in meaning to hateful.

clue.text: One kept in during school interval

indicators.note: detained, so the numeral is held within the phrase for during school

parts.note: in term means while school is sitting
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pupil gets detention during school break time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept in' sounds like detention but puts I inside IN TERM.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim is a period between two events, an interval.

clue.text: Service vehicles assembled for widespread communication

parts.note: Mass is a church service
media, plural of medium, are means or vehicles of expression

explanation.surface: Church minibuses gather for a big public broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vehicles' suggests cars or buses but means channels of expression; 'assembled for' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers, radio and television reach a vast audience at once, which is communication on a wide scale.

clue.text: Disaster when vehicle reversed by new driver into river

indicators.note: the reversed vehicle and learner go inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

indicators.note: the word for the vehicle is written backwards

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle
L is a learner driver, from the L-plate

explanation.surface: A learner backs a car into a river, with disastrous results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' fits the driving scene but turns CAB to BAC; with L it goes into DEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a humiliating collapse or failure, a disaster.

clue.text: Shoots vessel up, causing halt

indicators.note: in a down clue the whole run of letters is read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: to pot an animal or bird is to shoot it
a sub, submarine, is a vessel

explanation.surface: Someone fires at a ship that comes up, and it stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the whole of POTS SUB in this down clue. 'Shoots' looks like plant growth but means fires at.
explanation.definitionFit: A halt is a minor stopping place on a route, which is what a roadside stop for buses is.

clue.text: The start of a book collection

definitions.text: The start of a book collection

parts.words: The start of a book collection
parts.note: the opening volume of the Bible, a collection of books, whose name also means the origin of anything

explanation.walkthrough: 'book collection' looks like a library, but is the Bible, a collection of many books.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means origin or beginning, and it names the first book of the Bible.

clue.text: One observing exponent of gamesmanship

definitions.meaning: someone who watches out for things, such as birds or trains
Stephen Potter wrote Gamesmanship (1947), the guide to winning by psychological ploys

explanation.surface: A sports watcher turns out to be skilled at gamesmanship.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephen Potter's humorous book Gamesmanship gave the language that word; his initial and surname run together give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane-spotter is an observer, and the author S. Potter championed the art of winning by gamesmanship.

clue.text: Examination put back to end of August

indicators.note: the word for put is written backwards

parts.note: to set something down is to put it

indicators.note: only the final letter of August is used

explanation.surface: An exam is postponed until late August.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' looks like postponed, but 'back' reverses SET to TES.
explanation.definitionFit: A test is a trial of knowledge, an examination.

clue.text: Subject of Crown in charge

parts.note: the crown of the head is its top

explanation.surface: A loyal subject of the monarch is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject' looks like a citizen under the Crown, but it is a theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the matter under discussion, the subject.

clue.text: Excited outburst from supporter in violent disturbance

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
taken as written
a storm is a violent atmospheric disturbance

explanation.surface: A fan gets carried away during a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' suggests a fan, but means an undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainstorm is a sudden fit of mental excitement or frenzy, an outburst.

clue.text: Press club

definitions.meaning: to press clothes is to smooth them with a hot ...

explanation.surface: A newspaper's social club.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironing is pressing clothes flat, and irons are metal-headed clubs used in golf.

clue.text: Gallant beginners to brave Everest are unafraid

indicators.note: the beginnings, or first letters, of the following four words are taken

explanation.surface: Climbers who attempt Everest are fearless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gallant' looks like an adjective for the climbers but is the noun, a dashing man.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau or gallant is a fashionable man who pays court to women.

clue.text: Plant to flavour pea broth, not a stew

indicators.note: to stew is to cook in a mixed-up mess, so the remaining letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letter a is the part removed, signalled by not

explanation.surface: A cook adds a herb to pea soup instead of making a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' takes A out of PEABROTH; 'stew' jumbles what remains, PEBROTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A potherb is a leafy plant grown to flavour soups and stews.

clue.text: Hand in dictionary left out

indicators.note: the hand goes inside the dictionary

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: A word was missing from the dictionary handed in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something omitted has been excluded or missed, simply not included.

clue.text: Takes appropriate, remedies, applied externally

indicators.note: like an ointment put on the outside, the remedies wrap around the outside of the word for appropriate

parts.note: cures are remedies
apt means appropriate or suitable

explanation.surface: A patient takes suitable treatments, rubbed on the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'applied externally' reads like instructions on an ointment tube, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To capture is to seize or take by force, so captures means takes.

clue.text: Girl to go with rail trip

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl joins a railway outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' looks like a journey by rail, but it rearranges GORAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloria is a girl's name, an example of a girl.
